steps: Placement & floor support

Level surface that carries the fireplace and venting, out of traffic. Not directly on carpet, tile or other combustibles except wood flooring: use a metal or wood panel the full width and depth; build a solid, continuous platform if raised.

• No floor protection required in front; a combustible hearth extension is allowed. The fireplace bottom must be level with the finished hearth for the safety barrier to fit.
  • Portrait barrier B36-PTF2: fireplace 3" (76mm) above the finished hearth.
  • Approved for aftermarket, permanently located manufactured homes (USA only) or mobile homes where local codes allow.
  • Outdoor covered installs (pp. 17–18): operation approved 40°F to 110°F; overhang and its width to each side at least 1/2 the roofline elevation above the fireplace base; black painted barriers recommended.
The manual also prints the portrait barrier as #B36-PFT2 (p. 11); pp. 10 and 19 and the parts list (p. 60) give B36-PTF2.
Stand-offs & nailing flanges

Form and fit the top stand-off brackets and heat shields before setting the unit in the opening; mount the nailing flanges (¼" side clearance to framing). Top stand-off zone: non-combustible material only, full width.

1. Remove and save the (4) screws on the stand-off heat shields and brackets on top of the fireplace.
  2. Bend the top stand-off brackets at the perforations; secure with those (4) screws plus the (4) on top of the fireplace.
  3. Form the stand-off heat shields (flange up, toward the back); secure with (8) screws from the components packet.
  4. Move the (2) nailing flanges from the sides to the outside corners, stand-off flanges facing away; screw through the slots, bend at the perforation until parallel with the face.
  5. Set the framing studs against the small stand-off on the back of each flange; nail or screw.
Trim kit #B36-FTK and the exterior trim kit (B36-RSF2 only) attach before fireplace installation (pp. 22–23). Never permanently remove the nailing flanges.
Frame the enclosure
Rough opening 42" H × 36-1/4" W × 15-7/8" D in nominal 2" × 4" framing with a single vertical header board. Frame the vent pass-through keeping 1" clearance around the pipe.

• Measure from the fireplace floor level to the vent centerline; frame the wall opening so the vent runs level through the pass-through, adjusting for the elbow height of the vent system used.
  • Vent clearances: 1" (25mm) on all sides of vertical pipe; 1" top, sides and bottom of horizontal pipe.
  • Horizontal runs through walls: #700-WPT (walls 4" to 6½"; its heat shields overlap at least 1-1/2") or a thimble meeting the 1" top clearance. Thimbles and attic shields may take unfaced non-combustible insulation (ASTM E 136).
  • Metal Fab: adapter #4DDA adds 3-3/4" (95mm) to the vent centerline height and, rear venting, to the enclosure depth.
  • Don't recess the vent cap into the wall or siding.
Non-combustible zone & mantel
Fit the supplied 37-3/4" × 10-1/2" non-combustible board (3/4" lap onto the framing sides, 1/2" onto the header) and hold the trim, mantel and sidewall clearances and the minimum chamber heights.

NG rear vent, min chamber height45-1/2" (1156mm)
Top vent min. horizontal, rigid pipe50" (1271mm)
Top vent min. horizontal, flex pipe55-1/2" (1410mm)
The manual also prints 45-1/2" as 1556mm (p. 19 and the p. 20 footnotes); the p. 20 figures give 45-1/2" (1156mm).
  • Finish: dry, dust-free board; heat-resilient tape, mesh and joint compound (such as Durabond), cured per its maker; high-quality acrylic latex primer and finish coat, avoiding flat or light-colored paint.
  • Safety barriers mount per Section 4.4 (pp. 24–25); the bottom frame piece must be installed for them.
Gas line connection

Run the line through the left or right gas line hole to the ½" control valve inlet with a listed tee-handle shut-off and flexible connector (licensed plumber or gas fitter in Massachusetts). Check all connections for leaks with soapy water.

• Ships for natural gas. For propane, convert first with kit LCK-B36G-SPB, following its instructions.
  • Supplied: 3/8" (10mm) × 18" (457mm) flexible gas connector and manual shut-off valve. Don't route the line where it would obstruct the fan.
  • Inlet supply: NG 5" – 10.5" WC (7" recommended); propane 12" – 13" WC.
  • Disconnect the appliance for system pressure tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa); isolate it with its shut-off at ½ psi or less.
  • High altitude: consult the local gas distributor or authority having jurisdiction for rating methods.
Vent connection

Rear vent (NG only): finish the collar conversion first. If restricting the exhaust, insert the restrictor before attaching vent pipe; fit the vertical vent heat shield on every top vent (plus the horizontal shield for minimum horizontal runs) and keep 1" clearance to the pipe.

• Rear conversion (pp. 29–30): move the 4" exhaust and 6-5/8" intake collars to the rear and fit the cover plates on top, gaskets in place. Don't proceed with the installation until it is complete.
  • Restrictor, if used (p. 32): bend the tabs to about 80° and slide it into the exhaust on top, tabs toward you.
  • Heat shields (p. 33): vertical shield with (2) screws in front of the flue outlet; horizontal shield on its (3) tabs, 1" stand-off tab resting on the pipe.
  • #700-2 flex kits (p. 41): top vent only; 6" minimum bend radius to center; don't stretch an extension kit beyond 6'.
  • Provide a way to visually check the vent connection after the fireplace is installed.

Terminations (pp. 27–28)

  • Vertical cap, minimum height above the roof by pitch: 1.0 ft (flat to 6/12) up to 8.0 ft (over 20/12 to 21/12).
  • US horizontal: 12" above grade, 9" to a window or door that opens, 3' above a mechanical air inlet within 10' (Massachusetts: 10'). Canadian values differ.
  • Massachusetts sidewall terminations under 7' above grade: hard-wired CO detector with alarm and battery back-up on the appliance's floor, and a "GAS VENT DIRECTLY BELOW. KEEP CLEAR OF ALL OBSTRUCTIONS" plate at least 8' above grade in line with the terminal (p. 7).
Glass media
Set the glass media dam in the correct channel for the fuel, then spread the media one layer deep on the media tray and pilot shield. Never block the pilot.
Electrical & accessories
Grounded three-prong plug; 120VAC supply hot at all times with no switch. Install the (6) halogen light-kit bulbs and, if ordered, the #IPI-075 fan.

• Propane units: complete the gas conversion before installing the light kit.
  • Light kit (p. 46): remove barrier, glass, media, media dam and the (7) media tray screws; loosen the (4) light bar screws, tip the bars up and fit the (6) bulbs. Never touch the bulbs with bare hands.
  • Fan #IPI-075 (qualified installer): remove media tray, light kit and control board (p. 44); seat the fan on the studs at the back of the firebox with (2) flange nuts; connect it to the IFC module leads and plug in the cord.
Initialize the controls

Rocker switch OFF, 4 AA in the backup holder, 3 AAA in the remote, AC connected. Press SW1 (3 beeps, amber LED), then the remote ON/OFF within 5 seconds (4 beeps, pilot lights); press ON/OFF again, then set the rocker to ON.

1. Remove all packaging and combustible material from the firebox.
  2. Set the main ON/OFF rocker switch to OFF. Install (4) AA batteries in the backup holder and (3) AAA in the remote. Connect the IFC module to AC power.
  3. Press the red SW1 button: (3) beeps and an amber LED, ready to sync.
  4. Within (5) seconds press the remote ON/OFF key: (4) beeps, code accepted, pilot ignites automatically.
  5. Press ON/OFF again: the pilot goes out, confirming the command. Set the rocker switch to ON for remote operation.

Pilot mode, with the system off: mode key to the CPI icon, up arrow = CPI, down arrow = IPI. Manual operation without the remote (Section 10.3): rocker OFF, SW1 until 3 beeps, SW1 again within 5 seconds; the pilot lights and the rocker then runs the burner on HI only.
Pressure test & flame tuning

Check inlet (IN) and manifold (OUT) pressures with a manometer. Burn at least 15 minutes, then tune flame appearance with the venturi air shutter or the restrictor plate, letting the unit cool between adjustments.

Factory venturi openingNG 1/8" (3mm) · LP 5/8" (16mm)
  • Dark orange flame with black tips: venturi closed too far, open slightly.
  • Short, blue flames: venturi open too far, close slightly.
  • Lifting (ghosting): venturi closed too far or gas pressure too high; open slightly, check manometer.
  • Short, flickering (excessive draft): add restrictor. Lifting or ghosting (insufficient draft): remove inner ring(s) or the restrictor.

Venturi adjustment is for a qualified service technician; slight changes give dramatic results. After venting, the 4" exhaust is reached through the fireplace baffle ((3) screws). If flames still lift after opening the restrictor and verifying the vent, shut off the gas and call a qualified service technician.

items: Power interrupted or disconnected → restore power or use battery back-up
Wiring disconnected → check every connection against the wiring schematic
Gas off, no propane or low pressure → check all shut-offs; consult plumber or gas supplier
Pilot flame not reaching the flame sensor → adjust pilot screw on the valve, then seal it

items: ON/OFF rocker switch OFF → set to ON
Gas off or low supply → check for multiple shut-offs and the propane tank
Faulty or incorrect wiring → check and correct
Plugged main burner orifice → remove blockage

items: Vent cap incorrect or blocked; horizontal pitch under ¼" rise per foot
Inner vent pipe leaking exhaust into firebox, or excessive draft → repair; adjust restrictor

items: Venturi air shutter needs opening slightly → Section 11.2.1
Vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked → adjust; remove debris
Vent leaking or horizontal pitch wrong → repair; ¼" rise per foot

Two failed ignition tries; check gas is on and sensor not shorted, then reset or re-initialize

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
Your fireplace lights itself: an igniter sparks the pilot, and the pilot lights the burner. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Everyday start

  1. With the fireplace off, press the ON/OFF key on the remote.
  2. The fireplace beeps once. About 4 seconds later it starts sparking at the pilot, and the burner lights.

First start, or after the gas was shut off

  1. Read the safety information on the lighting page of the manual.
  2. Press ON/OFF so the fireplace is off, then turn off all electric power to it.
  3. Find the manual gas valve your technician installed. Turn it clockwise to OFF, by hand only, never with tools. If the valve won't turn by hand, don't try to repair it. Call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.
  4. Wait 5 minutes, then smell for gas, including near the floor. If you smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps.
  5. Turn the valve counterclockwise to ON, turn the power back on, and press ON/OFF.

To turn it off

Press ON/OFF. Before any service, also turn off the electric power and turn the manual valve clockwise to OFF.

If it doesn't light, it tries twice, then stops (a lockout). Press ON/OFF to turn it off, wait about 2 seconds, and press it again. If it still won't run, turn off the gas and call your service technician or gas supplier.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The Proflame 2 remote runs the fireplace. It takes 3 AAA batteries, which come with the fireplace. A single beep from the fireplace confirms it got a command.

Flame height

There are 6 flame levels. With the fireplace on, press the down arrow to lower the flame one level at a time, all the way to off. Press the up arrow to raise it. If the flame is off, the up arrow relights it on HI.

Thermostat

  • Press the thermostat key and the remote works as a room thermostat. Set the temperature with the arrows.
  • Press it until SMART shows, and the fireplace turns the flame down as the room reaches your set temperature. You can't set the flame by hand in this mode.

Fan and light (if installed)

Press the mode key to reach the fan or light icon, then use the arrows. Each has 6 settings.

Handy extras

  • Key lock: press the mode key and the up arrow together to lock or unlock the keys. A lock icon shows while locked.
  • °F or °C: with the fireplace off, press the thermostat key and the mode key together.

sounds.title: That sound or smell is probably normal
sounds.html:
Foggy glass

When you first light the fireplace, condensation forms on the glass. That's normal in all gas fireplaces and clears after several minutes.

A paint smell in the first hours

The paint cures during the first few hours of burning. Leave the fan off during that time to help it cure faster.

Ticks and pings

The metal expands as it heats and contracts as it cools, which can make noise. This is normal and doesn't affect how well the fireplace works or how long it lasts.

Blue flames at first

On a first lighting the flames look blue, then gradually turn yellow during the first 15 minutes. If they stay blue, or turn dark orange with black tips, have a qualified service technician adjust the burner.

Beeps

One beep confirms a remote command. A low double beep when you press ON/OFF means the backup batteries are low.

Fan still running? In thermostat mode the fan waits 5 minutes after the fire lights, to let heat build, and keeps running about 12 minutes after the fireplace turns off.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
The manual lists cleaning the glass as a once-a-year homeowner job. Only do it when the fireplace is completely cool.

  1. Clear a flat, stable work area big enough to lay the glass assembly down.
  2. Lift the safety screen up and out. Pull the 2 spring-loaded latches at the bottom of the firebox out and down, then lift the glass assembly up off the 2 tabs at the top.
  3. Clean the glass with a suitable fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and be careful not to scratch it.
  4. Hook the slots at the top of the glass over the tabs, lower it into place, and pull the latches out and up to lock it.
  5. Put the safety screen back before you use the fireplace.
Don't run it with the glass removed, cracked or broken. Avoid striking or slamming the glass. Replacement glass comes only as a complete assembly from the manufacturer and should be fitted by a qualified service person.

modes.title: Pilot modes: IPI and CPI
modes.html:
The pilot is the small flame that lights the burner. Your fireplace can run it two ways, and you pick with the remote.

  • IPI (spark-to-pilot): the igniter lights the pilot each time you turn the fireplace on, and the pilot goes out when it's off. With the fireplace on, the remote shows no snowflake icon.
  • CPI (continuous pilot): the pilot stays lit. It keeps the firebox warm and gets air moving up the vent, so the burner lights with less disturbance. With the fireplace on, the remote shows a snowflake icon.

To switch

  1. With the fireplace off, press the mode key until the CPI icon is selected.
  2. Press the up arrow for CPI, or the down arrow for IPI. A single beep confirms.

Why the pilot went out on its own

  • In CPI mode, if the burner hasn't lit for 7 days in a row, the pilot shuts off. It's a standard safety feature. Each time the burner lights, the 7-day timer starts over.
  • Within 24 hours of continuous pilot flame, the system turns itself off for about 5 seconds to run a safety check, then repeats your last command.
Pilot won't go out? It's set to CPI. Switch it to IPI.

power.title: Power & batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on 120V house power, with a battery backup so the burner still works in a power outage.

Backup pack (control module)4 AA, not included
Remote3 AAA, included

During an outage

  • The backup batteries run the burner only. The optional fan and light won't work until power returns.
  • How long the batteries last depends on their quality, how many times the fireplace lights, and other factors.

Low-battery signs

  • Remote: a battery icon appears on its screen. Replace the batteries and the icon goes away.
  • Backup pack: a low double beep when you press ON/OFF. After that, the fireplace won't accept commands until you replace the batteries. It beeps once when the new ones have power.
Not responding to the remote? Low batteries in the remote or the backup pack are the first thing to check.

media.title: Caring for the glass media
media.html:
Your fireplace's flames burn over a bed of glass media: glass beads or crushed glass spread on the media tray.

Why it changes

Direct heat and flame can discolor the media or leave a fine oily film on it. That's a natural reaction, and the media can be cleaned.

Cleaning the media

  1. With the fireplace off and fully cool, remove the safety screen and the glass (see Clean the glass).
  2. Wearing protective gloves, take the media out of the firebox.
  3. Wash it with mild dish soap and water. Drain and rinse it thoroughly.
  4. Make sure it's completely dry before it goes back on the media tray.
  5. Spread it one layer deep, the way it was installed.
Keep the pilot clear. Never let media cover the pilot. A blocked pilot can cause delayed ignition.

Don't substitute other materials. Your dealer can supply replacement media. Soot on the glass can mean the media isn't placed correctly, so have it checked.

service.title: Annual service
service.html:
Have a professional service person inspect the fireplace before use and at least once a year. Homes with a lot of lint from carpet or bedding may need more frequent cleaning.

What the service visit covers

  • Firebox, yearly: vacuum out debris, and check that the bottom glass latches move freely and still have spring tension.
  • Fan, every 6 months (if installed): disconnect power and vacuum it. The bearings are sealed and need no oil.
  • Vent system, yearly: inspect it. Nothing may block the flow of combustion and ventilation air.
  • Glass, yearly: clean it and check for cracks, scratches and nicks, replacing the assembly if needed.
  • Burner and pilot, yearly: vacuum, check the gas parts for leaks, and confirm the burner lights within 4 seconds and burns steadily.
Healthy flames are lazy and yellow, and steady, not lifting or floating off the burner.

Between visits, keep the area around the fireplace clear of anything that can burn, and of gasoline and other flammable vapors and liquids.

safety.title: Safety and gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building right away.
  • Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Before lighting, smell around the fireplace, including near the floor: some gas is heavier than air and settles there.

Around the fireplace

  • Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • The safety barrier (screen) protects children and others at risk from the hot glass. Keep it on. If it's damaged, replace it with the manufacturer's barrier for this fireplace.
  • Watch young children closely in the same room. A safety gate can keep toddlers away from hot surfaces.
  • Keep clothing and anything flammable off and away from the fireplace.
  • Never burn wood, coal, paper or cardboard in it.
Been under water? If any part of the fireplace has been under water, don't use it. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect it and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg. warrants to the original purchaser, from the date of purchase, that your Kozy Heat fireplace was free of defects in materials and workmanship when made. The warranty isn't transferable.

30 days · parts and laborPaint, light bulbs, gasket material, glass media and media dam
Year 1 · parts and laborAll other parts and material
Years 2 to lifetime · parts onlyFirebox, heat exchanger, logs, burner tube or pan, outer shell, heat shields, front glass (thermal shock only), refractory liner (not enamel or glass panels)

Labor is reimbursed to an authorized dealer only. Keep your proof of purchase with the serial number and model. If you notice a defect, contact your authorized dealer within 30 days.

What voids or limits coverage

  • Not installed by a licensed, authorized technician, or not installed, run and maintained as the manual says
  • Serial number or testing label removed, or the fireplace altered or tampered with
  • Submersion in water, or long periods of dampness or condensation
  • Installation and operating problems such as environmental conditions, inadequate venting or negative air pressure
  • Chimney components and non-Hussong accessories
This is a summary. The full terms and exclusions are in the manual.

Manufactured for natural gas. Convert with the kit and its own instructions, per ANSI Z223.1 and the authority having jurisdiction; on propane units complete the conversion before installing the light kit. Kit and orifice part numbers: p. 60.

High altitude

US: above 2,000' (610m), reduce input ratings 4% for each 1,000' (305m) above sea level. Canada: above 4,500' (1,372m), reduce the certified high altitude rating 4% for each additional 1,000' (305m).

specInlet.html:

Propane12" – 13" WC (2.99 – 3.24 kPa)

Test at the IN tap (A): loosen the screw, attach a manometer with a ¼" (6mm) I.D. hose, light pilot and burner with all other gas appliances in the house on. Out of range: contact the gas company; only a qualified gas service technician adjusts incoming pressure. Re-snug the screw and confirm the tap reads no pressure.

Disconnect the appliance and its shut-off from the supply piping for system pressure tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa); at ½ psi or less, isolate it by closing its manual shut-off.

specManifold.html:

Lifting ("ghosting") flames can mean gas pressure is too high: check the manometer settings.

Restrictor plate

Ships with both inner rings in (most restriction); knock out the innermost ring for less, all rings for least. Short, flickering flames (excessive draft): add restrictor. Lifting or ghosting (insufficient draft): remove inner ring(s) or the restrictor.
